Beach Clubs

Sunbeds, sea-level kitchens and the long afternoon · 29 venues, best rated first

Art Cafe

Beach Clubs · Agios Prokopios (clifftop, above the bay)
★ 4.7 235 reviews €€ 1.1 mi · 4 min from Plaka Beach

Not a beach club at all but the best sunset seat above Agios Prokopios — a quirky, eclectic cafe-bar perched on the cliff edge with a two-seat 'lovers' corner' hanging over the water. Over five hundred Naxian and Greek products line the shelves, and the crowd is a happy mix of locals, long-stay regulars and anyone who stumbled up the path at the right hour. Come for the golden hour, stay for the live music.

A Naxian citron liqueur or Greek craft beer in the cliff-edge corner, with a plate of island cheeses
Walk-in; phone ahead if you want the cliff-edge table at sunset

Del Mar Cafè

Beach Clubs · Agios Prokopios
★ 4.6 (Tripadvisor) 595 (Tripadvisor, via its FAQ page) — final.json had 591, so the count is still ticking up, which is itself a sign of life reviews €€ 1.4 mi · 4 min from Plaka Beach

The Italian outlier on a strip of Greek beach clubs, run with real warmth by Angela and Marco just a step back from the sand. There is no attitude and no cover charge — order a plate of house-made tortelloni and the sunbeds out front come free. It is the value play on Agios Prokopios and the locals' lunch of choice.

Spaghetti carbonara or the homemade gnocchi, washed down with Angela's mojito
Phone; reserve a table to secure the complimentary loungers and umbrella out front

Paradise Beach Cafe

Beach Clubs · Agios Georgios (Saint George)
★ 4.6 (Tripadvisor) 83 (Tripadvisor) reviews €€ 4.8 mi · 12 min from Plaka Beach

Old-school Saint George at its most likeable: a family operation where Manolis and his relatives run the floor, the food is fresh and local, and loungers cost about four euros. There is nothing designed about it and that is precisely the appeal — you can settle in at nine in the morning and still be there for the sunset. Vegetarian and gluten-free eaters are looked after without fuss.

Whatever fish is fresh that day, with a €4 lounger and a full afternoon in front of you
Walk-in; reservations accepted in person
Map

Finikas Club

Beach Clubs · Agios Georgios (Saint George)
★ 4.5 (Tripadvisor) 71 (Tripadvisor) reviews €

A superbly sited little cafe-bar right on the Saint George sand, best known as the breakfast spot before the beach fills up. Vegan and vegetarian options are handled properly, the staff are genuinely friendly and the bill is the friendliest on the beach. No pretensions, no DJ, no minimum spend.

Breakfast on the sand with a freddo espresso before the crowds arrive

Nomad Beach Bar Restaurant Naxos

Beach Clubs · Plaka (north end)
★ 4.4 415 reviews €€€ 0.0 mi · 0 min from Plaka Beach

An eco-chic beachfront sanctuary from the team behind 520 in Chora, built from wood, straw and earth tones with a farm of their own supplying the kitchen. The cocktails are among the most accomplished on the island and the portions are absurdly generous — gluten-free eaters are unusually well served. Take the third row rather than the first: the waves reach the front beds on a windy afternoon.

Watermelon salad and lamb chops with one of their custom rum cocktails; the pizza is made on site
Online request form on their site, phone or WhatsApp. Pre-booking sunbeds is strongly advised in August.

Macao Beach Naxos

Beach Clubs · Agios Prokopios
★ 4.3 1,011 reviews €€€ 1.4 mi · 4 min from Plaka Beach

Tulum with a Greek accent: raw timber, rope and bleached linen strung along the sand, with South-American-inflected Naxian cooking and a sushi counter that genuinely delivers. The sunset service is the whole point here — the umbrellas face straight into the western horizon and the whole terrace turns gold at once. Book the front row in August or accept the third-row view.

Flambéed salmon or a fresh sushi roll with the Macao Spritz; half-price classic cocktails at happy hour

This is the island's only true nightclub and, happily for you, the only room on Naxos where rap and R&B are the main event rather than a novelty. Sunset drinks on the open seafront terrace slide into an indoor floor that fills after one and doesn't empty until the ferries start moving — Greek drill and trap MCs, R&B selectors and funk DJs rotate through the season. Expect a young, loud, gloriously unpretentious crowd and drinks that are priced for a captive audience.

Gialitissa Boat Trips

On the Water · Panermos beach pier, south-east Naxos (past the palm trees, small pier 30m along the path)
★ 5.0 125 reviews from €25 per person (children €10; private group of 10 from €280) 28.0 mi · 63 min from Plaka Beach

A traditional wooden caique, a captain who grew up in this bay, and €25 for the most photogenic two hours on Naxos. You swim right inside Rina Cave – cold, echoing, lit turquoise from below – then anchor in a cove no road reaches. If you only do one boat trip on the island and want it short, cheap and unforgettable, this is it.

Three fast boats – a 12m Zen 39 and two 10m ribs – that turn Naxos into a launchpad: Koufonisia before lunch, Amorgos in the afternoon, Mykonos for dinner if you fancy it. ★ 4.9 3 reviews from $520 per group (up to 4 people) 4.2 mi · 9 min from Plaka Beach

A short, sharp private boat run to the Marianna wreck lying in the channel between Naxos and Paros – close enough to the surface that snorkellers get the full ghostly outline. Add the islet of Parthena and the pale sand at Kastraki and you have three of the best hours in the water on this island. Divers and non-divers both catered for.

Jason Daily Cruises

On the Water · Agia Anna port, Naxos
★ 4.8 697 reviews from €45 per person (from $104 on GetYourGuide) 0.7 mi · 2 min from Plaka Beach

'Jason' is an 18-metre wooden boat hand-built in Syros, and it feels like it – varnish, shade, the smell of grilling souvlaki drifting off the stern. The day runs from the sea-cave at Rina to the uninhabited beaches of Kato Koufonisi and finally into Koufonisia's whitewashed port for an ouzo. The single best-loved boat day on Naxos, and the one locals send their own visitors on.

Forty-five minutes out of Chora and you are stepping onto Delos, birthplace of Apollo, with three hours to walk the mosaic floors and the terrace of lions before the meltemi picks up. Mykonos in the afternoon is the deliberate contrast – cocktails in Little Venice, then home in the dark. The classic Cycladic double bill, and the cheapest way to do it.

The island's slickest fleet of Lagoon catamarans – Danae, Rena, Anassa, Steve π and Paciphae – slides out of Chora at breakfast and spends the day drifting between the Naxos and Paros shores. Nature and Art

Anastasia Maraki weaves on the loom at the back and sells what the family farm and hives produce at the front, which makes this the most complete little shop in Halki. Table runners and scarves off her own loom sit beside Naxos honey, home-set marmalades, capers, olives and hand-painted marble. Ateliers & Gifts · Eggares
★ 5.0 51 reviews €86-€1350 5.2 mi · 10 min from Plaka Beach

Naxos has been sending marble into the world since the Archaic period, and Maggie Ross is the person who will put a chisel in your hand and let you take some of it home. The studio is an open garden past Eggares — worktables under trees, a rack of hand tools, a block of white island marble each — and over three and a half hours you cut a relief from an Archaic template or your own design. Tools, marble and a spread of local bites and drinks are included; the thing you carry out you made yourself.

Your own carved marble relief · small marble pieces from Maggie's shop

Phos Gallery

Ateliers & Gifts · Halki
★ 4.8 10 reviews €€-€€€ 10.4 mi · 20 min from Plaka Beach

Phos means light, and Dimitris Gavalas opened this small white room in his father's mountain village during the worst of the crisis, on the theory that Halki deserved a gallery. The work is mostly black and white — island portraits, stone, symmetry, a cinematic patience that comes of years spent working alongside Theo Angelopoulos. A framed print is the least touristy thing you can carry off this island.

Eggares Olive Press Museum

Ateliers & Gifts · Eggares
★ 4.8 (Tripadvisor) 454 (Tripadvisor) reviews €5-€30 9.8 mi · 20 min from Plaka Beach

Fifteen minutes north of the port, in a green valley of olive groves and wild herbs, a family have restored an 1884 press — one of the oldest surviving on Naxos — and made it a place to taste rather than merely look at. Nikoleta walks you through the stone and the screw, then pours: plain oil, infusions, tapenade, olive bread, olive cake, even olive-oil ice cream. The shop is small and the buying is easy.

Naxos extra virgin olive oil · herb-infused oil · olive paste · olive-oil soap · olive wood spoons

★ 4.7 (Tripadvisor) 21 (Tripadvisor) reviews €3-€40 5.2 mi · 11 min from Plaka Beach

Opened by Ioannis Tziblakis in 1945 and now in the hands of his grandson, this is the old-fashioned Naxian pantry: shepherds' cheeses stacked behind the counter, olives in brine, thyme honey, capers, beans, spices in sacks, and extra virgin oil from the family's own groves. There are hand-made baskets and ceramics too, and ointments and soaps the family still blends. Labelling is sparse; ask, and you will be told exactly who made what.

A phytotherapy house built entirely on Naxian flora, with every eau de parfum, balm and candle named for a place on the island — Alyko, Melanes, Chalki, Filoti, Sangri. Vallindras Kitron Distillery

Ateliers & Gifts · Halki
★ 4.1 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json 212 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json reviews €8-€25 10.4 mi · 20 min from Plaka Beach

The oldest kitron house on the island, distilling citron-leaf liqueur behind the shutters of a Halki mansion since 1896 and still run by the fifth Vallindras generation. Copper stills, ledgers, gold medals from Marseilles and Bordeaux and the original 1860s equipment sit exactly where they were left, so the tour is less a museum than a working room that never got tidied. The free tasting runs white, green and yellow in ascending order of nerve.

Green-label kitron, 30% · white kitron, 33% · yellow kitron, 36% · miniature gift trio

Fish & Olive Gallery

Ateliers & Gifts · Halki
★ 4.9 (TripAdvisor, Aug 2026) - unchanged from final.json 352 (TripAdvisor, Aug 2026); final.json's 356 is a Google-side count reviews €25-€480 10.4 mi · 20 min from Plaka Beach

Katharina Bolesch throws and glazes the ceramics, Alexander Reichardt makes the silver and bronze, and together they have turned a corner of Halki's square into the most serious craft address in the Cyclades since 2000. The motifs never stray far from olive branch, fish and wave, but the drawing is loose and confident and the glazes are quietly beautiful — work that has travelled to Tokyo's National Art Center and to The Deep in Hull. The gallery holds the larger pieces; the boutique a few doors along carries linen, ceramics and prints you can actually get home.

Naxia Natura

Ateliers & Gifts · Halki
★ 5.0 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json exactly 172 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json exactly reviews €4-€40 12.9 mi · 28 min from Plaka Beach

A husband-and-wife shop on the Halki through-road that has quietly become the island's best-loved place to buy edible things — olive oil poured for tasting, mountain herbs, spices, teas, and honey from their own hives. Nothing is packaged to impress; everything is explained. It is ranked first of all shopping in Halki and deserves the twenty minutes it will take from you.

Naxos extra virgin olive oil · wild mountain tea · thyme honey · oregano and sage bundles · herb blends
Walk in; the owners will open bottles for you to taste.

Shelves of Naxian honey — thyme, wildflower, heather — plus propolis, beeswax cream and a wall of more than sixty spices, teas and mountain herbs, all weighed out by hand. The room smells of oregano and warm wax before you have crossed the threshold. This is the pantry stop that turns a Halki afternoon into a shopping list.

Naxos thyme honey · heather honey · propolis tincture · beeswax cream · wild oregano · hazelnut praline with honey

Manolis Lybertas Pottery

Ateliers & Gifts · Damalas
★ 4.7 (Google via Wanderlog, Aug 2026) vs 4.6 in final.json - but see the caveat below, the two figures may not describe the same listing 307 (Google via Wanderlog, Aug 2026) vs 92 in final.json - same caveat reviews €8-€80 11.3 mi · 21 min from Plaka Beach

In a low stone workshop in Damalas, Manolis Lybertas throws the shapes his great-grandfather threw: the sfouni wine jug, the perforated tyromethira used to drain cheese, and faithful reproductions of museum pieces. He works while you watch, wet-handed and entirely unbothered, and will explain what each vessel was for on a Naxian farm. Nothing here is decorative for its own sake, which is precisely why it looks so good on a shelf in London.

Sfouni wine jug · tyromethira cheese-draining pot · small olive bowl · museum-copy amphora
Walk in — the workshop is open daily until late evening and visitors are welcome to watch him throw.

Morfes Ceramic Workshop

Ateliers & Gifts · Chora
★ 4.6 (TripAdvisor, 9 reviews) - exactly the 4.6 / 9 already in final.json, independently confirmed. No change. 9 (TripAdvisor), unchanged reviews €10-€90 5.1 mi · 12 min from Plaka Beach

Efi Tzouma makes ceramics through the winter and opens the door in the alleys of Chora's old market for the summer, which is exactly the right order of operations. Glazed pomegranates for luck, espresso cups in a dozen colours, ceramic jewellery — small, personal, unrepeated. She wraps everything as though it has to survive a shipwreck, and if you are travelling light she will send it on for you.

Glazed ceramic pomegranate · espresso cup pair · ceramic pendant · small dish
Walk in during the season; the shop is in the old market lanes and keeps shop hours rather than fixed ones.

Tyrokomia Naxou

Ateliers & Gifts · Chora
€6-€35 5.3 mi · 11 min from Plaka Beach

The Koufopoulos family dairy keeps a shop on Papavasiliou, the food street that runs inland from the Chora waterfront, and it is where you go for the graviera that made this island's name. Wheels aged two to five years, the ash-rolled arseniko, the honey-cured melipasto, the unsalted graviera that tastes of grass and nothing else. Buy vacuum-packed and it will cross Europe without complaint.

Naxos graviera, aged 2-5 years · arseniko in ash · melipasto, cheese in honey · unsalted graviera · Cheese of Ariadne
Walk in; ask for it vacuum-sealed for the flight home.

Pagonis Greek Sandals

Ateliers & Gifts · Chora
★ 4.4 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json 32 (Tripadvisor) — matches final.json reviews €40-€180 5.3 mi · 11 min from Plaka Beach

The Pagonis family have been cutting leather on Naxos since 1940 and are now in their third generation, with two shops on Old Post Office Street and a workshop behind. Choose the model, the hide and the colour and they will make the pair to your foot overnight — the same procedure that produced the traditional Naxian shoe long before anyone called it a Greek sandal. Bags, belts and wallets come out of the same bench.

Custom-made leather sandals · traditional Naxian shoe · hand-stitched belt · leather travel bag
Walk in and be measured; custom pairs are usually ready the next day, so go on your first afternoon, not your last.

Tereza of Naxos

Ateliers & Gifts · Chora
★ 5.0 (TripAdvisor, 19 reviews) - matches final.json exactly 19 (TripAdvisor) reviews €45-€120 5.4 mi · 12 min from Plaka Beach

A tightly edited Greek concept store in the Faraggas lanes of the old town: handmade jewellery built from freshwater pearls, Murano glass and coloured stone, Cycladic marble pieces, linen dresses and a few very good candles. The house line — the fylachto earrings, the little fish pendants — is designed here and reads as Aegean without ever tipping into fancy dress. Everything ships worldwide, which matters when the good pieces are the fragile ones.

Fylachto earrings · Psari fish pendant necklace · Selini pearl necklace · Cycladic marble figure
Walk in when the boutique reopens each spring; the online store runs all year.

Katerina Vasilaki Handmade Jewellery

Ateliers & Gifts · Chora
★ 5.0 (TripAdvisor, Aug 2026) - unchanged from final.json 22 (TripAdvisor, Aug 2026); final.json's 23 is the Google count reviews €30-€200 5.5 mi · 12 min from Plaka Beach

Right inside the Kastro walls, next door to the Archaeological Museum, Katerina works sterling silver and shell into pieces that are never quite repeated — which is the point, and why she can make you something to order if you come back the following morning. Her daughters contribute straw hats and sandals, so the shop reads as a small family workroom rather than a boutique. Open unusually late, which makes it a good post-dinner detour.

Silver and shell earrings · one-off silver ring · hand-plaited straw hat
Walk in; commissions and adjustments are usually turned around next day.

Yalomorfon Glass Art Studio

Ateliers & Gifts · Galanado
★ 4.9 (TripAdvisor, 17 reviews) - exactly the 4.9 / 17 already in final.json, independently confirmed. No change. 17 (TripAdvisor), unchanged reviews €15-€150 4.8 mi · 10 min from Plaka Beach

The only fusing-glass workshop on Naxos, out at the Galanado turning where nobody stops by accident. Sheets of coloured glass are cut, stacked and taken through the kiln into plates, panels, crosses and small mosaic pieces; the owners will happily show you the process and take a commission. Careful, obsessive packing means the fragile things actually reach home.

Fused glass plate · glass wall panel · small mosaic piece · commissioned design
Call ahead or drop in — hours are short and it is worth confirming before driving out.
